notes.title: Graffiti Bombing - Update! (20 January 2025)
notes.content:
A new game build has been published, see the full release notes for details on the changes, updates and fixes etc.

[b]Release Notes:[/b]

[list]
[*] New(Screen Space FX): added more post processing effects to main player camera.
 - Shadows (SSS): enabled by default, as saves performance, manage in settings.
 - Ambient Occlusion (SSAO): more expensive, enabled on high graphics, manage in settings.
[*] Improve(Temporal Anti-aliasing): added quality level control to settings.
[*] Improve(LOD Bias): various adjustments to the way bias is handled.
 - Adjust all game models to use 1 as the default bias factor.
 - Expose the bias as a setting on player home TV menu.
 - Use default value of 1, unless on a very powerful rig.
[*] Improve(Open World): various optimizations and performance improvements.
 - Optimize and reduce polygon count for all 3D models.
 - Optimize vegetation, reduce tree complexity, improve impostors.
 - Add LOD group and levels to all exterior models by default.
 - Add impostors to all other models that give a good result.
 - Reduce number of LOD levels, improve culling distances.
 - More performance optimizations and improvements coming later!
[/list]

[b][u]Note:[/u] all game settings have been reset with this update, as new options added, and graphics configurations adjusted. A reset like this will happen only on a rare occasion.[/b]

[i][u]Support GB:[/u] If you’re enjoying the game, please consider leaving a review on Steam—it’s a great way to assist the project and helps us continue improving!![/i]

notes.title: Graffiti Bombing: Early Access Update - January 2025
notes.content:
[b]Welcome to 2025, GB Crew![/b]

We’re excited to announce that [i]Graffiti Bombing[/i] is officially back in Early Access on Steam!

It’s been a long road—full of challenges, learning, and hard work—but the journey has been worth it. When I started back in 2016, I barely knew Unity or VR development. Today, after years of growth and dedication, [i]Graffiti Bombing[/i] is finally back and better than ever.

But this isn’t the end—it’s a new beginning. Over the next 1–2 years, we’ll be expanding the feature roadmap, building on the solid foundation now available to play for free on Steam.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36170835/e7dc815607420a530817f0b9b7c3fdf2c842557b.jpg[/img]
[i]Image above - fresh new piece at the road bridge tunnel by [b]_Korbo_[/b] (Instagram: @korb_crazyapes)[/i]

[h3]Current Game State & Features[/h3]
[i]Graffiti Bombing[/i] is back with a strong foundation and plenty of features to get you started:
[list][*] [b]Game Areas:[/b] Access to the Player Home, Open World starting area, and Creative Sessions maps for focused painting experiences.
[*] [b]DLC Content:[/b] The `All City Edition` DLC adds extra paint types, tools, and features, with more exclusive content and areas coming in 2025.
[*] [b]Core Mechanics:[/b] Single-player gameplay, locomotion, and object interactions are stable and functioning well.
[*] [b]V1 Paint System:[/b] Graffiti tools like spray cans, paint rollers, and marker pens are fully supported and improved.
[*] [b]Player Home:[/b] The home base is polished and functional, with room for future updates.
[*] [b]Open World Zones:[/b] Level loading and zone mechanics work, though lower-end systems may experience performance issues or bugs.
[*] [b]Creative Sessions:[/b] Single-map environments are ideal for players on lower-end systems.
[*] [b]Multiplayer & Player Customization:[/b] Planned for 2025—stay tuned for updates![/list]
[i]As expected, you may encounter bugs or performance issues, especially on lower-spec systems. We’ll be actively collecting feedback to fix problems and improve the experience throughout Early Access.[/i]

[h3]Intro & Quick Start (Tutorial)[/h3]
Missed the basics? No worries! Here’s the [b]Intro & Quick Start[/b] tutorial video to help you get started.

You’ll also find this video playing in-game on the [b]TV screen[/b] in the [b]Player Home[/b] during your first run of the new [i]Graffiti Bombing[/i] version.

[previewyoutube=D2kkxCcA77Y;full][/previewyoutube]
[h3]Early Access Features In Development[/h3]
January is all about polishing, fixing bugs, and optimizing performance. Even better, [i]Graffiti Bombing[/i] is now running on the Unity 6 Engine, bringing cutting-edge technology to power the project.

I’m already working on new features and have big plans for the coming months. I’ll also be gathering ideas and feedback from the community to help shape the roadmap.

See the list below for some of the currently planned features coming during Early Access:
[list][*] [b]GRAF-CAM:[/b] A video director system for placing virtual cameras to record and replay graffiti sessions.
[*] [b]Multiplayer Mode:[/b] Collaborate online with friends to bomb locations together.
[*] [b]Open World Expansion:[/b] More bombing zones and locations, accessible via subways, sewers, and hidden routes.
[*] [b]V2 Paint System:[/b] A more realistic, physics-based paint system with improved features and fixes.
[*] [b]Advanced Paint Zones:[/b] Save, load, share, and import graffiti; aged and weathered effects over time.
[*] [b]Challenge Modes:[/b] Objective-based gameplay with hazards, health, and AI-driven graffiti scoring.
[*] [b]NPCs and AI:[/b] Populate the world with NPCs, adding dialogue and interactivity.
[*] [b]Social Media Integration:[/b] Expanded sharing options to showcase and promote your creations.
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36170835/2eb1e12be43a1c32c76dc1119fbca2f401262ca1.jpg[/img]
[i]Image above - amazing Halloween beta piece at the old warehouse interior by [b]SEY[/b] [/i]

[h3]Community[/h3]
Your feedback and ideas are what keep [i]Graffiti Bombing[/i] growing. Share your thoughts through the Steam Community forums—I read every post and reply where I can.

Want to connect directly with the dev team or chat with other writers? Join our Discord server to get involved, share ideas, and even get access to beta versions in the future.

Join us on Discord: [url=https://discord.gg/ZVkByeVyQG]https://discord.gg/ZVkByeVyQG[/url]

[h3]Special Thanks[/h3]
I'd also like to send a special shout out—in no particular order—to:
[list]
[*] [b]All the beta testers[/b] – for helping to test builds, send feedback, and share awesome graffiti pieces.
[*] [b]Vandal[/b] – for testing, great feedback and ideas, graffiti contributions, and helping to mod Discord.
[*] [b]PrEeNnIoSb[/b] – for helping run the beta, providing support, and also modding Discord.
[*] [b]SEY / Player A / _Korbo_[/b] – for creating awesome graffiti and letting me use it on the Steam store.
[*] [b]All City Edition crew[/b] – for buying the DLC and helping to support the project!
[/list]

[i]Thanks for all your support so far—I can’t wait to hear what you think of the new version. Grab your spray cans, get creative, and let’s go bombing![/i]

[b]// Wildstyle @ Graffiti Bombing[/b]

notes.title: Graffiti Bombing: Development News - July 2023
notes.content:
[b]Hey GB Crew![/b]

So it's been a long while since my last community update, however development work has continued on GB. At the moment we are in closed beta testing, with a group of testers from the  [url=https://discord.gg/UM4nyT7]GB Discord server[/url].

The beta testers have been testing the new player home area and improved VR interactions systems. Along with the various other new features and improvements that have been made to the game, since I took it of Steam and rebuilt everything from the ground up.

[i]In case you missed it - here is a  video preview from the end of 2022, that shows off the current state of the game and demos the new VR interactions system.[/i]
[previewyoutube=ly2aGTxD0Sw;full][/previewyoutube]
The plan for GB remains pretty much the same - continue development and implementation of new and improved features, until we get to a point where the beta testing group think the game is ready for release back into Early Access on Steam.

[b]Main tasks remaining before relaunch.[/b]
[h3][/h3]
[olist]
[*] V2 Paint System updates (in progress).
[*] Actions Assistant improvements (in progress).
[*] Basic director camera system.
[*] Open World mode optimizations (in progress).
[*] Creative mode implementation.
[*] Performance optimizations.
[*] Steam store / branding / marketing updates.
[/olist]
Realistically the remaining work listed above will take another 2-3 months to complete, test and finalize. However I remain committed to the project and am definitely planning to relaunch back onto Steam in 2023.

Once we get back onto Steam in Early Access - then work on the game will continue for another 1-2 years, or until the game is ready to go to a full release. One of the main features to be added later being multiplayer... it is coming!

[h3]V2 Paint System Updates[/h3]
About two months ago, I made the decision to start work early on the V2 paint system. The V1 line drawing algorithm had a number of major setbacks and issues, plus it was not easy to extend or add new features.

So I've re-written the line drawing algorithm ready for the V2 paints system. The result is a much better spray line that looks more realistic and the spray caps dynamics are now starting to feel different per cap type, which is what we want.

I've also added some new paint features, such as spray mist droplets, which surround the line as you spray. Along with splatters, which are random bits of paint that can sometimes happen. These new settings are all configurable from the paint system settings.

Additionally the undo system has been completely re-written and is now much better and more reliable. You can also configure the number of undo / redo steps to a maximum of 10 steps, via the game settings.

[i]See the new V2 line drawing algorithm (WIP) in action, via the video embedded below.[/i]
[previewyoutube=AHMUhvGYpio;full][/previewyoutube]
Worth noting, that the V2 line algorithm is [u]not yet final[/u], however it's already a BIG improvement on the V1, and a really solid base / starting point that we can build on, and add more features to in the future.

[h3]New TV Main Menu System[/h3]
The new main menu system is available on a large curved TV screen that is in the player home. You can pick a remote control from the table and manage all the Open World game instances, Creative Sessions and Settings etc.

This new menu is much easier to use, and I'll be adding more features to it in the future.

[i]See a preview of the new TV Main Menu System, via the video embedded below.[/i]
[previewyoutube=AK-tbIaErMg;full][/previewyoutube]
[h3]Community[/h3]

As always - you can interact with us via the Steam community features. We do read all posts, and reply where and when it makes sense.

The Graffiti Bombing group on [url=https://discord.gg/UM4nyT7]Discord[/url] is open. So you can jump on there if you want to speak with the development team directly, or meet other potential players and graffiti artists. 

We'll also be taking more beta testers as we get closer to launch... so be sure to join the GB Discord server, if you'd like a chance of getting into the game early before relaunch!

Discord server: [url=https://discord.gg/ZVkByeVyQG]https://discord.gg/ZVkByeVyQG[/url]

[b]  [/b]

[b]// Wildstyle @ Graffiti Bombing[/b]

notes.title: Graffiti Bombing: Development News 2022 #2
notes.content:
Hey GB Crew!

Since the last update I've been head-down working hard on the road-map. Overall making good progress and really happy with how things are shaping up. Although some features are taking a bit longer to develop than expected, due to additional code complexity and a strong desire to make the VR interactions reliable and a more enjoyable experience.

Hopefully the wait will be worth it! Read on to get more details on the progress, including a few exciting new features coming to GB in 2022!!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36170835/f50945bb28dd8af665f1e6a38c00a11030aa0938.jpg[/img]
[i]Image above - improved quick color panels for paint tools.[/i]

[h3]Road-map Progress Update[/h3]
Completed quite a few of the items that were listed in the previous community update, also have added a few new things that were unplanned at that time, but required as I discovered along the way.

The following items are now mostly complete, or at least working in a fairly usable state.

[list]
[*] Completely new VR system, for more immersive movement and interactions.
[*] Reworking the player models hand system, re-rigged and improved physics.
[*] Interactive objects support multiple grab points and full gravity grab action.
[*] Re-working paint tools like the paint roller to be more user friendly, less glitchy.
[*] New inventory system will let you store a lot more objects, and easier to use.
[*] New interactable objects to stack and climb, also ladders and platforms.
[*] Integrate new / URP render pipeline to improve performance and customization.
[*] Rebuild paint surface shaders and integrate system for new render pipeline.
[*] New lighting system for more physically correct baked lighting with specular.
[*] Relighting all current scenes for the new lighting and rendering pipeline.
[*] Day / night improvements with new environment FX and street lamps etc. at night.
[*] New terrain vegetation rendering system, for better quality / performance.
[*] New player home area, first version that will be improved / added to over time.
[/list]
[i][u]Note:[/u] these features are not yet publicly available, there will be an official launch announcement![/i]

[h3]Video Updates[/h3]
See the videos below that demonstrate some of the new features and improvements. You can also see these videos and more on the [url=https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCI2IslKuiC51gPcLeZouAJw]GB YouTube channel[/url]. Subscribe for new videos coming each month!

[previewyoutube=jJyvGJhcm30;rightthumb][/previewyoutube]
[b]Better Interactions and Physics![/b]

Integrated a completely new physics based interactions system for 2022. Better physics and other features like different hand grab positions, climbing, gravity grab, and more realistic interactions with doors and other objects. Less glitching and more immersion!




[previewyoutube=WxgGfLgX8SE;rightthumb][/previewyoutube]
[b]Improved Spray Can Quick Color Panels![/b]

Major improvements to the quick color panels. You can now grab and re-arrange them next to where you are spraying or painting. Also can have multiple panels open at the same time, which makes for a better workflow when working on a big piece!




[previewyoutube=JY3ljgMWG2o;rightthumb][/previewyoutube]
[b]Player Home MP3 Jukebox![/b]

Created an interactive MP3 jukebox for the player home area. You can add the music files to a specified local folder, edit the playlist text file and then it will get automatically loaded next time the game starts. Customize your favorite playlists to listen to while you paint!




[previewyoutube=dJ6RzOrF8yw;rightthumb][/previewyoutube]
[b]New Backpack Inventory![/b]

The new backpack inventory is a big improvement - it looks better, is easier to use, and you can stash more items than before. Plus you can also stash items whilst wearing it, by dropping them into the backpack over your shoulder!




[previewyoutube=Tlbj0vSPjSc;rightthumb][/previewyoutube]
[b]New Climbable Objects System![/b]

Adding a new climbable objects system - a simple inventory belt on the player for stashing spray cans. A way to resize bigger objects like ladders and platforms, then stash them in your backpack. Take climbable objects with you when you paint. Arrange them, lock them and then climb up to reach those high spots more easily!



[previewyoutube=_dxITtE6V7Y;rightthumb][/previewyoutube]
[b]Improved Paint Roller and New Marker Pen![/b]

Much better physics and interactions makes the paint roller feel great, no more glitching out and it's quite fun to use! The new marker pen also feels pretty nice to use, and this is an early version... so more updates, pen and tip variations coming in the future!




[previewyoutube=I1nu_NrOGJA;rightthumb][/previewyoutube]
[b]Day and Night Improvements with Weather Systems![/b]

First test of day / night cycle with some simple weather patterns. Stuff gets wet too!

notes.title: Graffiti Bombing: Development News 2022 #1
notes.content:
Hey GB Crew!

If you joined the GB playtest on Steam - I hope you've been having fun, and are enjoying the improved experience and paint system updates. It's been great to see some of your cool graffiti creations and gather valuable player feedback via the GB Discord server.

The playtest is still open - so if you haven't already joined and would like to give it a try, you can sign-up from the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/561440/Graffiti_Bombing/]GB Steam store page[/url] and start playing right away. The current playtest version is the fully unlocked experience, as it is right now. So it's a good opportunity to try out the game and get up in VR for free!

[h3]Why so quiet, what's been going on?[/h3]

Yes, it's been a long while since I posted any updates to Steam, however work still continues on the game. Getting GB back into playtest in 2021 took a lot more effort than expected, including some major updates that we had to do to the V1 paint system.

That said, I think it was worth it. Feedback on the improved V1 paint system has been really positive overall. Performance-wise it's a big improvement and it's now possible to paint lag free mostly, even on lower end rigs that could not handle the game before.

However- even though the current GB playtest experience is much better, I still feel the game is not ready for releasing back into Early Access (EA). So my current plan is to leave the playtest open, until I get the game into a more solid state, one that is ready to release back onto Steam EA.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36170835/605aa7ae758a4de1396ea992581efe9a2e769dab.jpg[/img]
[i]Image above - new player home entrance through the sewers.[/i]

[h3]Development road-map for 2022[/h3]

I've been gathering player feedback on the playtest, adding items to a list for development. There are also some major updates of my own in the works, that I think will make a big difference to the overall experience, making it more stable and fun in VR.

Here is a list of what's being worked on right now:

[list]
[*] Completely new VR system, for more immersive movement and interactions.
[*] Reworking the player models hand system, re-rigged and improved physics.
[*] Interactive objects support multiple grab points and full gravity grab action.
[*] Re-working paint tools like the paint roller to be more user friendly, less glitchy.
[*] New inventory system will let you store a lot more objects, and easier to use.
[*] New interactable objects to stack and climb, also ladders and platforms.
[*] Integrate new / URP render pipeline to improve performance and customization.
[*] Rebuild paint surface shaders and integrate system for new render pipeline.
[*] New lighting system for more physically correct baked lighting with specular.
[*] Relighting all scenes, plus making the terrain lighting mixed for better performance.
[*] Day / night improvements with new environment FX and street lamps etc. at night.
[*] New terrain vegetation rendering system, for better quality / performance.
[*] New player home area, first version that will be improved / added to over time.
[*] New menu system for game setup, quality and other settings.
[*] New ways to play the game, open world roaming vs. single level painting.
[*] Various minor bugs and improvements gathered from the playtest feedback.
[/list]
Wow, there is a lot there! Yes there is - but the good news is that it's all doable, and that work actually started in November last year. So I've already completed some items from the list above, and am making good progress on the others.

These updates will roll out incrementally over the next 3-6 months, as there is a lot of changes happening. So it will likely be released on an experimental Steam branch to start with.

So this is why I'm now starting to update the Steam community again, and will be posting development updates on a monthly basis going forward. To keep you all updated on progress, as we get closer to releasing a new playtest version.

Also - depending how things go I may also start to record some development videos, to give previews and sneak peaks on the new features and updates as they get closer to completion. More info coming on this soon!

The Graffiti Bombing presence on Twitter has been quiet for some time now. Previously I was posting updates on the [url=https://twitter.com/UrbanWeaponry]Urban Weaponry[/url] account. However moving forward, I'll be switching to use a dedicated Twitter account for Graffiti Bombing, which you can find @ user [url=https://twitter.com/GB_Wildstyle]GB_Wildstyle[/url].

notes.title: Graffiti Bombing: Development News #5
notes.content:
Hey GB Crew!

We launched into Early Access around 10 days ago, and considering we'd been in beta for a few months before that, I'd hoped the launch would go fairly smoothly. However to be honest that's not the case, as you'll notice from the mixed reviews we received on Steam since launch.

That's OK though, we live and learn... and sometimes you don't always succeed the first time! So yesterday after careful consideration, I made the decision to take Graffiti Bombing off public sale and disable downloads.

I did this to give myself time to consider all the feedback received so far, make a plan to improve the experience, address bugs and handle the performance issues. At the same time we plan to put in place additional systems and optimizations, to handle cases where people with lower-end, below minimum spec systems (i.e. a potato) try to play.

[h3]What is Graffiti Bombing?[/h3]

To be 100% clear we're not trying to be a clone, or a copy of something else... we're looking to cut our own groove, and do things a bit differently. Yeah of course we're doing graffiti, however in the longer-term we are planning to offer something more, that is a bit unique.

The goal is to make an immersive, open-ended, free roaming graffiti experience, with a more physically correct paint system and tools, an experience that performs well across most high-end VR devices and decent computer setups.

Creating such an experience in VR is definitely a challenge, no doubt about that. However, even after the rocky start of the last week or so, we still think it's possible.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36170835/71f048c27f60aa5da43984bde0089cc929cbd786.jpg[/img]
[i]Image above - nearby Paint Zones highlighted in the train yard start area, FX changing in V2![/i]

[h3]Early Access development road-map for 2020-2021[/h3]

At this point we think it makes sense to openly share our plans for the first year of Early Access on Steam. There is a short-term and longer-term plan for development, which I'll outline below.

In the short-term - we intend to address as many of the launch issues we've seen, and get the project to a better place where we can relaunch and open things back up to the players. How long this will take is not clear right now, although I'd estimate 2-3 months, maybe even more depending how things go.

The longer term plans are more interesting - as they involve the new V2 paint system, along with a bunch of other new features and improvements that will really start to take the project forward. You can review a development road-map diagram below to see more details.

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36170835/47494daa57b4d37cef4b69400016465bc8386ce7.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36170835/47494daa57b4d37cef4b69400016465bc8386ce7.png[/img][/url]
[i]Click on the image above to see a full-sized version.[/i]

[h3]What's next?[/h3]
We'll be moving back into development on the items outlined in the diagram above. So things may get  bit quiet around here, however I'll keep posting community updates, and we'll start sharing more details on the new V2 paint system soon as well.

If you already downloaded or purchased Graffiti Bombing DLC, don't worry we are not deserting you! As we complete works on bug fixes, improvements and changes we'll be releasing interim patch updates, initially through the private beta channel on Discord.

If you are an All City Edition DLC player and not already on [url=https://discord.gg/UM4nyT7]Discord[/url], please join and hit me up on there. Then I'll give you a unique Discord role and invite you to the beta channels.

notes.title: Graffiti Bombing: Launch Date Confirmed!
notes.content:
Hey GB Crew,

You may have noticed the release date for Graffiti Bombing has recently changed to an actual day...

[h3]T-minus 7 Days Until Launch[/h3]

I'm happy to confirm it's official, we'll be launching into Early Access on Friday, 28th August, 2020!

That's not to say things are final and 100% bug free - however we are in a much better place than we were 4 months ago - and considering we are releasing Early Access, I cannot delay things any longer.

Getting to this point has been incredibly hard work, and so I'd like to thank all the supporters that gave encouragement and helped motivate me to keep going. Special thanks to the Discord crew and beta testers who have tested, given feedback, found bugs and offered their suggestions for improvement.

[h3]Early Access Plans[/h3]

This is just the start of the journey for Graffiti Bombing - we've got to the door and are about to open it, launching into Early Access on Steam!

Over the next 1-2 years we have a lot of plans and ideas for where we would like to take the virtual graffiti experience. For those of you that intend to join us on this journey, we look forward to sharing the ride with you, which should hopefully be a real mission of discovery, creativity and fun.

If things go to plan - by the end of Early Access, we'll have a graffiti art experience that we can all enjoy and be part of as a community for years to come. The best part of course is going to be the art, and I cannot wait to see what you all create with Graffiti Bombing and share in the coming months!

As a reminder, here are a few of the planned features for Early Access:
[list][*] V2 Paint system: a realistic, more physically correct spray paint system (more details soon).
[*] Additional Areas: more bombing zones and different locations to travel to and experience.
[*]Advanced Paint Zones: management for saving / loading / sharing / importing content etc.
[*]Custom spray caps configuration and a utility tool to help you create your own caps.
[*]Player Home: chill-out area / hub, complete with mini-games, media and social features.
[*]Play Modes: full version offers three different modes of play - Creative, Challenge and Multiplayer.
[*]Community Content: SDK / tools for content creators to help create their own locations / zones.
[*]GRAF-CAM: video director system, allows placing of virtual cameras for in-game recording.
[*]Social Media: more types and different sharing options, to get your content noticed.
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36170835/a7b79cb19e938849b892c962e7b45f647d7655ad.jpg[/img]
[i]Image above - lift area exit from the underground bunker base (All City Edition DLC).[/i]

[h3]VR Hardware Support[/h3]

Another thing to highlight now we are closer to launch are the various VR headset, controller setups that Graffiti Bombing supports, and that have been tested. Also to discuss some of the technical differences, configuration options, and performance considerations.

List of supported / tested VR hardware:
[list][*] HTC VIVE and Wand Controllers
[*] Valve Index and Knuckles Controllers
[*] Oculus Rift and Touch Controllers
[*] Windows Mixed Reality and Motion Controllers
[*] Oculus Quest (link cable or Virtual Desktop streaming) and Touch Controllers *
[/list]
[i][u]Note[/u]: items marked with a * are experimental support only at this time.[/i]

All headsets listed have a custom controller configuration setup and have been tested. Depending on the controller type the experience will default to a 'click to grab' or 'hold to grab' style, i.e. on the Knuckles it defaults to a 'hold to grab style'. You can override the preferred grab style in the game options. Button configurations also change slightly depending on the connected controllers.

Performance varies slightly depending on the hardware, as does the accuracy of the movement tracking. Room-scale tracking setups with base stations are of course more accurate. If you are on a headset with inside-out tracking the level of tracking accuracy is noticeably different, particularly when drawing outlines for example. We do plan to revisit in the V2 paint system and see if there are ways to smooth out the tracking accuracy more for devices that use inside-out tracking.

Oculus Quest support is experimental at this time, and only with the link cable or via Virtual Desktop streaming. Initial beta builds showed poor performance with the link cable, and although it has improved in recent builds, the performance is still not good enough to say we officially support the headset. If you use the link cable then expect to dial down quality settings and tweak your configuration to get things playable. Virtual Desktop streaming in comparison seems much better, as long as you have a fast WiFi setup I would recommend this approach. The experience and performance with Virtual Desktop streaming is very playable on our test systems.

[h3]Feedback & Bugs[/h3]

Building great software is not easy, and creating VR experiences that are glitch free and without bugs is nearly impossible. That said, we are committed to making the Graffiti Bombing experience as solid and bug free as possible. However, it's going to take time and a lot more work to achieve this goal.

As we launch into Early Access I'd like you to consider and understand that we are still in a beta phase of sorts, as that is how we are viewing Early Access. You will encounter bugs, and possibly performance issues, depending on your computer rig and VR setup. Make sure your computer specs meet the minimum requirements to run Graffiti Bombing, also ensure your systems are patched and all drivers up-to-date etc.

If / when you do encounter issues the best thing you can do is report it back to us. Then I assure you that we'll investigate and try to fix it. We'll prioritize bugs in order of severity and will release regular patch updates for any critical issues that may arise.

Please understand though, that fixing bugs takes time - particularly difficult or hard to recreate issues - so I thank you for your patience in advance and ask that you bear with us for the first few weeks after launch.

Note: you can report any bugs or issues direct to the development team at:
[url=support@graffitibombing.com]support@graffitibombing.com[/url]

[h3]Community[/h3]

As always - you can interact with us via the Steam community features. We do read all posts, and reply where and when it makes sense.

The Graffiti Bombing group on Discord continues to grow, and now has more than two hundred like-minded people that are into VR, graffiti and street art! So you can jump on there to meet other potential players and artists.

Note: that we'll be adding more community setup and features to Discord in the coming months.

Discord server: [url=https://discord.gg/ZVkByeVyQG]https://discord.gg/ZVkByeVyQG[/url]
---

I look forward to seeing you soon in Graffiti Bombing!

// Wildstyle @ Graffiti Bombing

notes.title: Graffiti Bombing: Development News #4
notes.content:
Hey GB Crew,

It's been a while since the last update, apologies for the radio silence!

Rest assured, we are still alive and working hard on development for GB - however it's taking a lot more work to get ready for launching into Early Access.

[h3]Closed Beta Update[/h3]

The first beta group started in May 2020 with a small group of testers. See the list below for some relevant details.[list][*] Current build supports hardware for HTC VIVE, Valve Index and Oculus Rift.
[*] Testers have been doing graffiti, testing the tools and exploring environments.
[*] Providing valuable feedback for improvements on features and usability.
[*] Reporting bugs and glitches, that we have been able to track and fix.
[*] Providing valuable hardware specific feedback on controller configurations.
[*] Helping us to work through performance and bugs related to hardware.
[*] Contributing new ideas and suggestions that will make the experience better.
[/list]

Thanks to all the beta testers so far - your time in testing, reporting bugs and sending valuable feedback is much appreciated!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36170835/aa203338e151964f918f3d2beb06013d807fa482.jpg[/img]

[i]Image above - very first GB piece from the amazingly talented [b]-noRMSter-[/b][/i]

[b]  [/b]

[h3]Development Progress Update[/h3]

After launching the beta it became clear how much work is left to-do before GB will be ready for Early Access. Considerably more than previously thought! However, this is a good thing overall - the feedback, bug fixes and improvements that we are continuing to work on now, will make the GB experience better in the long-term.

The current development focus has been adjusted to follow the beta feedback. More performance optimization and improvements are required - so the last 1-2 weeks have been spent working on that, with a goal of making the experience run better across all supported VR / hardware / platforms. Also reducing the memory footprint, and we've made some decent progress. In the next beta build the memory usage has been reduced by around ~40% which is quite a bit!

There are always trade-off's though in software development - you improve / change one thing and it can affect something else. This is true for performance too, as to reduce the memory overhead the only way to do that effectively, is to load / unload graphical assets and levels more often. This can result in some performance spikes when loading a lot of data, however overall I think the trade-off and performance gains are worth it.

Development tasks for the rest of June:[list]
[*] Fix all bugs and feedback reported to-date by the first group of beta testers.
[*] Continue to improve World streaming - relates to scene and zone load / unloading.
[*] Add more configuration and performance options for graphics / quality.
[*] Minor adjustments to the V1 paint system, also add some more cap types.
[*] Improve interactions, add more grab options for different controller types.
[*] Add hardware support for Oculus Quest (link cable setup only).
[*] Add hardware support for Windows Mixed Reality setups (experimental support only).
[*] Improve the in-game tooltips system and add more help options.
[*] Finish the DLC integration and get the Early Access build ready.
[/list]

[h3]What's Next[/h3]

Well - we cannot delay things forever! So are continuing to work hard toward the next planned launch window, at the end of June 2020.

In the next 1-2 weeks we'll be announcing a second phase of the beta testing, and invite more people to join that and have a chance to try out GB. If you're interested in becoming a beta tester, you can [url=https://forms.gle/qbaMDqMStdNEhsER8]sign-up using the Google form here[/url]. Please note, you'll also be required to join the GB channel on Discord, so we can set you up as a tester.

There is quite a bit of interest in the project right now, which is awesome! It's surprising how many people from all walks of life are interested in the graffiti / street art culture, and that motivates us greatly. I'm really looking forward to seeing what you all create, once we finally get GB launched into Early Access.

[h3]Community[/h3]

As always - you can interact with us via the Steam community features. We do read all posts, and reply where and when it makes sense.

The Graffiti Bombing group on [b][url=https://discord.gg/ZVkByeVyQG]Discord[/url][/b], continues to grow. So you can jump on there if you want to speak with the development team directly, or meet other potential players and graffiti artists.

Discord server: [url=https://discord.gg/ZVkByeVyQG]https://discord.gg/ZVkByeVyQG[/url]

[b]  [/b]

Thanks for your continued patience and support!

notes.title: Graffiti Bombing: Development News #3
notes.content:
Hey GB Crew,

Ain't no joke - we are actually getting closer to the first round of user testing!

[b]Development Progress Update:[/b]

I've been working hard on finishing up critical functionality and tasks, then fixing bugs mostly. Moving any non-critical tasks to post launch, so back in the ice-box for now.

Current tasks left in progress, before the first Steam test build is published:[list]
[*] Testing across different VR setups for first round of beta (HTC Vive, Valve Index and Oculus Rift).
[*] Fixing any critical issues for device types, mostly button mappings and orientation  tweaks.
[*] After that I'll be starting to get the first beta build ready for Steam to review.
[*] Then will setup a beta channel on Discord, start inviting people, and give some beta info.
[*] Finally start sending out the first test build via Steam, initially to a small group of testers.
[/list]

Depending how much critical feedback, and how many bugs come out of the initial testing phase, will affect the timeline to launch into Early Access. As soon as the base game and features are stable / playable enough, I'll look to the initial public Steam release.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36170835/0ed0e49a2b8905ea651091c2e3b347e43299116c.jpg[/img]

[i]Image above is the new paint roller, which is physics based and quite fun to use.. but still a bit glitchy![/i]

In other developments...

[b]New paint system V2:[/b]

The current V1 paint system in Graffiti Bombing works well, but has some hard limitations.. as such it's not physically correct in all situations. Some planned future functionality will be too hard to effectively implement in the V1 paint system, or it will not work 100% reliably and be difficult to maintain. Plus there are various edge-case and bugs that are proving difficult to solve. This is due to the underlying design / architecture, and limitations that have only become apparent as I've got further into development.

Considering the goal of Graffiti Bombing is to be a more open-ended / open-world level design experience, realizing the full potential of the paint system is critical to the long-term enjoyment and success of the project. Looking forward to the next year or so of Early Access on Steam - I'm happy to announce that we have already started working on a V2 of the paint system, which is a complete rewrite and that will solve all the issues from V1. The new system is more physically correct and quite advanced, more details to follow soon.

Building the V2 paint system would not have been possible on my own. As such I will soon be joined on Graffiti Bombing code development, by a new developer who's expertise in graphics and shader tech, will allow us to realize the dream paint system we've all been looking for in VR. Together we will be focusing on the paint system rewrite as a priority over the coming months, and then will integrate into the Steam build on Early Access once ready.

[b]DLC Pricing Finalized:[/b]

Adding a new developer to the project of course comes at a cost, as previously I was the sole developer. However, I think it's worth it, for us to realize the full potential of Graffiti Bombing. As such I will be increasing the DLC cost to $12.99 USD as a way to help mitigate the increased development costs. This is not a change that I make lightly, and I hope that you can understand the reasons behind it, and give your support. If all goes to plan in the coming months, then you should eventually see this change as a positive thing, and start of the new revolution!

Launching on Steam - this will still be happening on the same timeline, much as possible. However early adopters should understand the V1 paint system will be replaced in the coming months. As we are launching Early Access on Steam, I think this should still be OK. Over the coming months we can also continue to work at improving level design and other systems such as interactions, interfaces and more, so it's going to be a busy time for us all once we get started!

As always - you can interact with us via the Steam community features. We do read all posts, and reply where and when it makes sense.

The Graffiti Bombing group on [b][url=https://discord.gg/UM4nyT7]Discord[/url][/b], continues to grow. So you can jump on there if you want to speak with the development team directly, or meet other potential players and graffiti artists.

notes.title: Graffiti Bombing: Development News #1
notes.content:
Hey GB Crew,

[b]Welcome to 2020 - a new era, and the official start of Graffiti Bombing on Steam![/b]

I'd like to share a brief project development / plan update with you. With a goal of giving you some more details and specifics about the work that is left to-do, before we can go to an initial release on Steam.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36170835/399868b57abbc7136f85fa45d8e76e0d9cc9fba5.jpg[/img]

As you've probably noticed, the current release date for Graffiti Bombing says January 2020, and here we are... it's January [i]already[/i], and wow that arrived so fast! To be clear -- the project is not quite ready to launch yet -- and it's very likely that I'll be moving back the release date to the end of February 2020.

That said however - I do want to launch as soon as possible, and definitely before Half-life Alyx, as it's going to be madness around that time (and I want to play that so badly myself too!).

So to keep you updated, here is the low-down / info on a few things...

[b]Graffiti Bombing Website:[/b]
Site design is built and first draft of content is ready. Waiting for the video to be complete and then the site will go live, planning for middle of January as well  (Edit: Delayed 1 week).

[b]Project Development:[/b]
As I've been preparing the promotional assets, graffiti and videos etc. for Steam, I've been playing the graffiti simulation quite a bit. This time spent has been really helpful for me to experience in-depth the graffiti tools, user experience and interactions etc. I've identified various things that require rework and adjustments, to improve and make the experience easier, more reliable and fun.

Current cards / tasks that need completing before beta:
[list][*][b]Spray cans:[/b] object grabs and interactions require improvement / bug fixes.
[*][b]Hand positions:[/b] need a way to adjust position as relates to spray can orientation.
[*][b]Spray caps:[/b] are working well, however need to add more types and FX.
[*][b]Spray can quick actions:[/b] UI requires tweaking / adjustment for usability.
[*][b]Paint system:[/b] more optimization and improvements for multi-canvas.
[*][b]Wall clean / fill / paint roller:[/b] systems requires more work and optimization.
[*][b]Load / saving:[/b] across paint zones requires more optimization and improvement.
[*][b]In-game help system:[/b] requires more content, images and video, plus another station.
[*][b]Free to Play vs DLC:[/b] full-game systems requires final integration and testing.
[*][b]Player calibration:[/b] system to calibrate the players height vs. object interactions.
[*][b]Performance:[/b] optimization and testing across supported VR hardware devices.
[*][b]Steam build:[/b] prepare for beta testing group, organize event and distribute build.[/list]

[/list]
